name: print.simplex
title: Print Solution to Linear Programming Problem

origin.description: Print method for an object of class simplex.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A simplex object returned by simplex.
Further arguments passed to or from other methods.

origin.details: The objective coefficients are printed. If an optimum was found, the solution and the optimal value are printed. If a feasible point was found but phase 2 hit the iteration limit, the last feasible solution and its objective value are printed. If no feasible solution could be found, that is the message.
origin.example:
# Print the diet problem from the simplex example.
enj <- c(200, 6000, 3000, -200)
fat <- c(800, 6000, 1000, 400)
vitx <- c(50, 3, 150, 100)
vity <- c(10, 10, 75, 100)
vitz <- c(150, 35, 75, 5)
print(simplex(a = enj, A1 = fat, b1 = 13800, A2 = rbind(vitx, vity, vitz),
              b2 = c(600, 300, 550), maxi = TRUE))

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A Simplex object returned by simplex.

translation.details: The objective coefficients are printed with R's digits=7 format. If an optimum was found, the solution and the optimal value are printed. The value in that sentence uses R's as.character. If a feasible point was found but phase 2 hit the iteration limit, the last feasible solution and its objective value are printed. If no feasible solution could be found, that is the message.
translation.value: The text that was printed. R returns x invisibly; the text is returned here so it can be compared.
translation.example:
from boot.simplex import print_simplex, simplex

# Print the diet problem from the simplex example.
enj = [200, 6000, 3000, -200]
fat = [800, 6000, 1000, 400]
vitx = [50, 3, 150, 100]
vity = [10, 10, 75, 100]
vitz = [150, 35, 75, 5]
print_simplex(
    simplex(
        a=enj,
        A1=fat,
        b1=13800,
        A2=[vitx, vity, vitz],
        b2=[600, 300, 550],
        maxi=True,
    )
)
